title: PPS as the space of the bodily self, back-space profile
citation: Noel, J.-P., Pfeiffer, C., Blanke, O., & Serino, A. (2015). Peripersonal space as the space of the bodily self. Cognition, 144, 49-57.
notes: Companion ready profile for Noel 2015 Experiment 2. It captures the reported back-space looming PPS task with back vibration and source-backed synchronous/asynchronous stroking block labels. Exact waveform, gain law, speaker switching, SPL, speaker model, and full sound-file offset remain original-author provenance gaps. A 100-ms derived terminal margin contains the existing software cue; it is not a reported trial interval or evidence of full-protocol timing equivalence.

reference_parameters.experiment_label: Experiment 2 back-space looming with back vibration
reference_parameters.software_trial_padding_basis: Derived containment for the existing software timeline: pre=0 ms; post=max(0,max(SOA)+cue duration-source duration)=1140+100-1140=100 ms. Noel et al. 2015 Methods 2.3.2 and 2.4: the last reported sound-relative cue is 1140 ms and lasts 100 ms; exact sound offset is unreported. The current 1.14-s premade clip is a software choice. The reported 0.5-s inter-trial interval and 10-s FBI period after each triplet are separate protocol requirements, not demonstrated by this containment margin.

provenance.source: Manual review records Experiment 1 as front-space looming toward chest and Experiment 2 as back-space looming toward back.
Manual review records T1-T6 at 190, 380, 570, 760, 950, and 1140 ms with D6-to-D1 looming mapping over 90-15 cm.
Manual review records Precision MicroDrives 100 ms vibration at stern level: chest in Experiment 1 and back in Experiment 2.
Manual review records synchronous and asynchronous visuo-tactile stroking as separate counterbalanced blocks for each main experiment.
Manual review records 72 PPS, 24 tactile-only baseline, and 12 auditory-only catch trials per stroking block.
